basis: SLC26A2-related skeletal dysplasias primarily affect bone and cartilage; other organ damage is not consistent across subtypes.
Carcinoma arising in skin with basal and squamous cytological features.
Congenital pituitary hormone deficiency with deficient central vasopressin secretion; no intrinsic renal damage established.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining T-cell lymphopenia in 5/5; pneumonia is a separate infection, and colitis occurs in only 1/5.
Benign epithelial neoplasm arising in the colon.
Severe intestinal malabsorption is defining, with protracted diarrhea in 30-79%; separately diagnosed respiratory infections and cholangitis excluded.
Progressive central neurologic disease with regression, spasticity and cerebral/cerebellar atrophy; oromotor dysfunction is neurologic.
Malignant granular cell tumor is a nerve sheath neoplasm of Schwann-cell origin; anatomical presentation varies.
Inherited encephalopathy defines brain dysfunction; additional organs vary across the constituent diseases.
Structural diverticula of the small intestine.
Adrenal cortisol excess causes muscle/bone loss in roughly 50-80% and skin atrophy in about half; separately coded hypertension excluded.
Alopecia universalis and severe intellectual disability define the syndrome.
Pulmonary hypoplasia is usual in this severe thoracic dysplasia; cystic renal dysplasia is common (~30% or more). Hepatic, cardiac and CNS lesions are mostly <30%.
Predominantly an ovarian neoplasm, outside the axes; rare pancreatic examples do not characterize most patients.
Contractures and kyphoscoliosis each affect 4/5, muscle atrophy 3/5; hypodontia in 3/5 also qualifies but is omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Viral infection directly involving ocular tissues.
Cerebral vascular amyloid causes recurrent brain hemorrhage and stroke in 80-99%; systemic deposits alone do not establish other organ dysfunction.
Renal hypoplasia/aplasia, scoliosis and ptosis each occur in 80-99%; severe intellectual disability defines the syndrome.
Genetically defined combined immunodeficiency; supplied evidence establishes no common intrinsic damage to additional organs.
Congenital lymphatic vessel hypoplasia causes chronic lymphedema; persistent hyperkeratosis and toenail dysplasia occur in 30-79%. Cellulitis is a separate infection.
Hepatitis A virus directly causes acute hepatic inflammation; arthralgia does not establish joint damage.
Localized congenital hair abnormality with frequent epidermal nevi; ocular and other extracutaneous abnormalities are uncommon.
Contractures occur in 20/20; optic atrophy and sensorineural hearing loss each in 30-79%. Frequent neurogenic bladder omitted because of the four-axis cap.
Cerebellar neurodegeneration defines the disease; optic disc pallor and esotropia each occur in 1/3. Central eye-movement signs alone do not establish ocular damage.
Neurodevelopmental impairment defines the syndrome; cardiac septal abnormalities and strabismus each occur in 30-79%. Renal abnormalities occur in <30%.
